apod.explanation: A crescent Moon and bright Venus appear together over Poland's Tatra Mountains at dusk in a planetary conjunction, with the bright star Spica — a triple star system about 250 light-years away in Virgo — just to Venus's left.
apod.title: Moon, Venus and Spica Meet

breaking.fact: Shares traded near $159 in premarket trading Thursday, down about 6% from Wednesday's $173.73 close, after the board met late Wednesday and announced no decision on ousting founder-CEO Jensen Huang; Bloomberg reports the board is working with an outside firm on successors and weighing an interim chief, and Dan Ives puts Nvidia at $300 a share with Huang vs $225 without him. Earnings are due Nov 17.
breaking.headline: Nvidia slides in premarket as board weighs Huang's future — no decision yet

breaking.fact: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow Thursday for talks with Vladimir Putin — Witkoff's 10th meeting with him — after two days of Abu Dhabi talks ended with a prisoner exchange agreed but no ceasefire; Kyiv has rejected Putin's demand to surrender all of Donbas, and mediators are steering toward security guarantees and reconstruction.
breaking.headline: US envoys land in Moscow for talks with Putin on Ukraine

breaking.fact: Initial claims rose 9,000 to a seasonally adjusted 200,000 for the week ended Nov 7, slightly above the 195,000 forecast, but claims have stayed at or below 200,000 since mid-September; continuing claims fell 20,000 to 1.697 million. October payrolls surged 165,000 and unemployment fell to 4.1%.
breaking.headline: Jobless claims edge up to 200,000, still a firm labor market

breaking.fact: Rain is likely in Houston on Sunday (80% chance, about 0.7 in) with a flash-flood risk NOAA rates level 1 of 4 — level 2 south of the city — and a cold front late Sunday drops Monday's high into the upper 50s; Saturday stays dry and partly cloudy. Parts of Texas have already had one of their wettest Novembers on record.
breaking.headline: Weekend storm: rain likely Sunday in Houston, cold front to follow

items.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two supertankers carrying more than 4 million barrels of oil combined were disabled by massive explosions late Wednesday after using what Iran calls an unauthorised southern route; Iranian state media said they hit naval mines. Reuters reports no independent confirmation of the cause, and the tankers' names, flags and crews have not been publicly identified.
items.headline: Two supertankers explode after hitting mines in the Strait, IRGC says

items.body: Kpler data reported by Reuters shows commercial cargo transits through the strait fell to 5 last Saturday, from 31 the week before, with none recorded Sunday, after ADNOC said three of its vessels were attacked; the IMO counts 133 confirmed incidents and 25 seafarer deaths since February, and is not advising ships to transit. Some vessels sail with AIS switched off, so the true count may be higher.
items.headline: Strait traffic collapses: 5 transits Saturday, none Sunday

hormuz.stats: Traffic & shares (latest verified): AIS-visible commercial traffic is running about 8% of normal — 6.9 ships a day over the past week (18 tankers) against 84.8 before the crisis. EIA puts Hormuz oil flows at 4.9M bbl/day in Q2 2026, down from 21.6M in Q4 2025; the IEA estimates ~20M bbl/day transited in 2025, about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade. China takes ~42% and India ~13% of strait crude throughput; ~90% of Iran's oil exports go to China. The EIA warns vessel-tracking data have become less reliable during the conflict.

marketsNote: Premarket Thursday: futures point to a lower open after Wednesday's rebound — S&P 500 futures -0.4% near 7,608, Nasdaq-100 futures -0.9%, Dow futures about flat — as Nvidia slides ~6% premarket to ~$159 after its board met with no decision on ousting CEO Jensen Huang. Oil eases (WTI ~$85.60, Brent ~$91.29) on peace-talk hopes; the VIX is back near 18.4 and the 10-year yield ~5.01% as bonds reopen after Veterans Day. Today: weekly jobless claims came in at 200,000; October existing home sales at 10 AM ET; Friday brings the PPI report.

space.body: NASA announced a round of new contracts worth $15 billion over ten years for its Moon Base program, including a $10 billion master contract under the Commercial Lunar Payload Services program and plans for a lunar rover using spare Mars hardware; eight companies will compete for payload missions as Administrator Jared Isaacman pushes the lunar outpost.
space.headline: NASA awards $15B in Moon Base contracts as lunar program accelerates

space.body: At its Oct 23 'Artemis Acceleration' briefing, NASA confirmed it has still not decided whether SpaceX's Starship or Blue Origin's Blue Moon will carry the crew on the first lunar landing, targeted for 2028 — the choice will ride on test results. The briefing also confirmed the Artemis II Orion heat shield performed as expected, with less cracking and char loss than Artemis I, and gave a first look at SpaceX's lunar Starship crew cabin.
space.headline: NASA still hasn't picked its Moon lander — Starship vs Blue Moon rides on tests

space.body: Salk Institute researchers built ASAP, a light-based tool that rapidly, precisely and reversibly turns autophagy — the cell's recycling process — on and off, revealing new targets including nuclear pore proteins and a link between protein building and breakdown. Published in Nature Cell Biology, the tool could expose disease-relevant targets in neurodegeneration, cancer and aging.
space.headline: Light-controlled tool switches cellular recycling on and off

weekInBrief.body: Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far above the 65,000 consensus, with September revised up to 60,000 and August up 53,000; unemployment fell to 4.1% and hourly wages rose 0.4% for the month and 3.1% over the year. The strong report, with hot CPI, has markets fully pricing a December Fed hike.
weekInBrief.headline: October jobs beat: 165,000 added, unemployment 4.1%

weekInBrief.body: UK GDP rose 0.7% in the third quarter, in line with forecasts and up from 0.5% in Q2, with September output up 0.2% against expectations of no growth; services expanded 0.9%, including a 2.1% rise in information and communication. Traders price a 76% chance of a Bank of England hike in December.
weekInBrief.headline: UK economy grows 0.7% in Q3 as AI investment offsets energy costs

weekInBrief.body: US mortgage rates declined for a fourth consecutive week, lifting home-purchase applications by the most since mid-April, as buyers respond to easing borrowing costs even while the Fed signals another hike in December.
weekInBrief.headline: Mortgage rates fall for a fourth straight week; home-buying jumps

weekInBrief.body: Nonfarm business productivity rose at a 3.6% annualized rate in the third quarter — output up 3.7% against hours up just 0.1% — while unit labor costs fell 0.7% and the labor share of output hit a record low 53.0% in data back to 1947. The BLS preliminary release is due for revision Dec 8.
weekInBrief.headline: Productivity surged 3.6% in Q3 as unit labor costs fell
